title: Adaptive column prioritization and hover-preview mode for large virtualized tables
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: introduce an adaptive column prioritization system and a lightweight hover-preview layer for rows in highly virtualized tables. This solves two user problems: 1) in narrow or high-density views, critical columns should remain visible while lower-priority columns collapse progressively, and 2) users should be able to inspect truncated cell content or inline aggregates without forcing a full row expansion or expensive reflow. The feature must work with continuous virtualization (infinite scroll), support keyboard navigation and screen readers, and align with current design tokens (spacing/density/color) so it can be toggled via density modes.

Scope: design tokens mapping for micro-density states, new column priority metadata in the table API, hover-preview surface that reuses existing popover components, accessible keyboard-first reveal (space/enter to preview), and a fallback for touch devices (long-press or tap-to-preview). Also includes UX for per-column filter chips that persist when column is collapsed and a small visual signal for columns that are hidden by prioritization.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype in Figma demonstrating 3 density modes (Comfortable, Compact, Micro) with adaptive column collapse rules and hover preview content for truncated cells.
- Interaction spec describing keyboard flow, screen-reader announcements, and touch fallbacks.
- Tokens mapping document tying density tokens to row heights, cell paddings, icon sizes, and tooltip spacing.
- Engineering checklist with performance constraints: hover-preview must not trigger full re-layout, and virtualization scroll jitter must remain below threshold measured in ENG-40211.
- Design review approved and a small A/B test plan defined for rollout to 10% of prod routes.

Constraints & trade-offs: we avoid live DOM expansion on hover to prevent layout thrash; the hover-preview should be an overlay that reads from the cached cell content or an async fetch for very large payloads. For very high-cardinality tables we will prefer truncated inline aggregates and allow the hover preview to show the full expansion only for selected rows to control rendering cost.
comments: 2026-02-20 — Kickoff: aligned with PM (Evan Torres) and Eng lead (Renee Hu). Agreed on problem statement and measurable success metrics (reduced user clicks to view full content by 40%, maintain 16ms frame budget on common scenes).

2026-02-24 — Design exploration v1 uploaded to Figma (link below). Two approaches: collapse-then-preview vs responsive-prioritization. PM prefers prioritization because it preserves column context for users with saved views.

2026-02-28 — Engineering feasibility review: ENG raised concerns about hover-preview reading large HTML blobs; recommended using a lightweight summary payload in the table rows and fetching full content on demand. Added dependency ENG-40211 for virtualization perf measurement.

2026-03-03 — Accessibility pass with Samira Gomez: confirmed keyboard-first flow and role=button on preview affordance is necessary; screen reader should announce 'preview available' when focus lands on a truncated cell. Added acceptance criteria for sr-only announcements.
2026-03-05 — Design crit: moved to a single shared overlay component to minimize DOM churn and reuse console popover styles. Decided on micro-density token set and updated spacing scale.
2026-03-09 — PRD updated with rollout plan and A/B test metrics; PM signed off. Preparing handoff artifacts for engineering spike scheduled in next sprint.
2026-03-10 — Prototype iteration v2 uploaded after addressing keyboard/accessibility notes. Need engineering estimate for API changes (column.priority metadata and preview payload field).
design_decisions: Use overlay-only preview to avoid layout reflow under virtualization
Expose column.priority in component props: high | medium | low | optional
Persist filter chips for collapsed columns in the filter bar rather than inline to maintain discoverability
Map micro-density to token set: ds-spacing-xxs / ds-font-12 / ds-icon-12
Keyboard interaction: focus -> press Enter/Space to open preview; Esc to close; Right arrow to move to next previewable cell
